read_this_way.note: LPA-D2 (2026-08-29): the pre-conversion header claimed batch-position resume-after-Ctrl-C — FALSE. lastParcelId was a local variable, never persisted. The TRUE property: idempotent, not resumable — ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING makes a re-run safe (no duplicate writes, no corruption), but every invocation re-scans the FULL parcels population from id > -1, whether the prior run got through 1 batch or 486. A full re-scan of 486,530 parcels costs the entire ~200s every time.

decisions.note: A-1 RULING (Fold A, orchestrator, 2026-08-29, within the pre-authorized plan): a new runMaterializePhase (a FORK of runCascadePhase's phase-order shape, NOT an extension of runLinkPhase — runLinkPhase's SELECT-then-batched-executeUpsertBatch write path would split this step's single server-side statement, breaking G2's verbatim guarantee) + LG-18 (executeInsertSelectNoRetract, INSERT-only structurally enforced). recovery.reset ships declare-only (no new destructive rebuild mechanism this pilot).

R-B/R-F item 1 (2026-08-29): this pilot's write has no destructive retraction target (class D, retract:"none"), so it does NOT exercise or close R-B's crashed/stuck-running reader gap — carried forward again to whichever future pilot first ships a genuine retract_when:"full_only" target. R-M's before_image and recovery.interrupted both ship "none"+why for the same reason: there is nothing to image or to interrupt.

Peel 8a (2026-08-29): R-B's carry is stated plainly as NOT EXERCISABLE HERE, not merely deferred by inconvenience — this step genuinely has no FULL mode to auto-force. runMaterializePhase (scripts/lib/step/index.js:1263-1272) returns a hardcoded mode:"incremental" on every RUN branch; staleness.fingerprint_inputs/mode_select:"none" (descriptor) means LINK_PARCEL_ADDRESSES_FORCE_FULL only bypasses staleness.ledgerGatedSkip's SKIP decision (bypassed flag, :1154) — it does not switch the batch loop onto a different code path, because the loop always re-scans the full parcels population from id > -1 regardless (LPA-D2: idempotent-not-resumable). A crashed/stuck-running auto-FULL reader has nothing to force this step INTO that a plain re-run does not already do. R-B's reader stays a genuine future obligation for a step whose FULL mode is behaviourally distinct from incremental (e.g. a retract_when:"full_only" target) — never satisfied by this pilot's shape.
